# Best waterproof Bluetooth speakers for the pool or beach

**JBL Charge 6 is the best all-rounder.** It's IP68, rated for 20 hours (28 with Playtime Boost), and doubles as a power bank. What Hi-Fi named it best overall, and Best Products rates it highly too. Prices ran about $130 at Walmart to $150 at Amazon. [Buy links at What Hi-Fi](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart) and [Best Products](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/).

**Other picks by need:**

| Need | Pick | Why | Where to buy |
|---|---|---|---|
| Loudest, for pool parties | JBL Boombox 4 | RTINGS' top pick. It floats, handles long immersion, and lasts 40+ hours. It sounds muffled off to the sides. | [RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth) |
| Even sound all around | Ultimate Ears Epicboom | IP67, floats, 360° sound, 15 hours. Tom's Guide's top pick. | [Tom's Guide](https://www.tomsguide.com/best-picks/best-waterproof-speakers) |
| Budget | Ultimate Ears Wonderboom 4 | IP67, floats, 14 hours. About $65–80. | [Best Products](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/) |
| Cheapest | JBL Go 5 | Pocket-sized, IP67, about $40, but only 8 hours of battery. | [What Hi-Fi](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart) |
| Easy to pack | JBL Grip | Can-shaped, IP68, 12 hours, $100. Good Housekeeping's best overall. | [Good Housekeeping](https://www.goodhousekeeping.com/what-to-buy/a71783745/best-waterproof-speakers/) |
| Big, floating party speaker | Soundcore Boom 2 Plus | 100 W, IPX7, floats, up to 20 hours. It's heavy at 3.8 kg. | [Soundcore via Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-boom-2-plus) |

The Boom 2 Plus is $249.99, or $200 with code AFSC20, which Dealectric tested in Soundcore's cart on Oct 22. The code expires 2026-12-31, and checkout has the final word. That link is an affiliate link, so Dealectric earns a commission. The other links go to review pages, so I can't confirm exact current retailer prices.

**Beach and pool tips:**
- Look for IP67 or IP68. Good Housekeeping suggests at least IPX7 for pool use.
- IP ratings don't cover salt or chlorine damage. Rinse the speaker with fresh water afterward if the manual allows it, and dry it fully before charging.
- Keep the charging port closed. Keep the speaker on a towel rather than in the sand, since sand can work into openings.
- The older Soundcore Boom 2 has no dust rating, so it's better for the pool than the beach.

If you tell me your budget and whether you need big party volume or something small, I can narrow this to one pick.
